kr-joseon.title: Royal Standard of the Joseon Dynasty
desc: - The Joseon Dynasty (1392–1897) royal standard featured a red field with the taegeuk (yin-yang) symbol and trigrams
- **Construction:** a white field, sometimes with dynastic emblems. The Joseon dynasty used plain white standards reflecting Confucian austerity
trivia:
- The Joseon Dynasty (1392–1910) ruled Korea for over 500 years
- Represented one of the world's longest-lasting dynasties
- Ended with Japanese colonization in 1910

kr-taegeukgi-1883.title: Original Taegeukgi (1883)
desc:
- The earliest known version of the Korean taegeukgi, used from 1883, featured the red-and-blue taegeuk (yin-yang) at the centre on a white field with four trigrams — similar to the modern South Korean flag but with different trigram arrangements
- Designed by Bak Yeong-hyo and first flown during his diplomatic mission to Japan in 1882, it was officially adopted on 6 March 1883 by the Joseon court
- **Construction:** a white field with a bicoloured taegeuk centred and four I Ching trigrams in the corners. Ratio approximately 2:3
trivia:
- The original Taegeuk flag from 1883 represented early modern Korea
- First used during Korea's diplomatic engagement with the West
- Evolved into the modern South Korean flag
